story.title: Cornell Faculty Votes No Confidence in Leadership Over Handling of Sexual Assault Case
story.summary: The Faculty Senate at Cornell University has passed a resolution expressing 'no confidence' in the university's leadership. This decision comes in response to criticism regarding the administration's handling of a sexual assault case involving a former student who alleged she was drugged and raped at a fraternity house in October 2024. Faculty members hope this vote will prompt the university's trustees to address perceived institutional failures.

This decision follows a civil lawsuit filed by the alleged victim against seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity, claiming she was drugged and raped at their house.

timeline_highlights.summary: Cornell University's president, Michael Kotlikoff, described the allegations of a gang rape involving a student at a fraternity house as 'deeply disturbing.' In a recent video statement, he emphasized the need for the university to improve its response to such incidents. The allegations have led to increased scrutiny of the university's handling of sexual assault cases, with the accuser, identified as Jane Doe, suing the university and several former students.

event_overview.title: About Cornell University Case
event_overview.subject: Cornell University Case
event_overview.summary: This event concerns allegations by a former Cornell University student that she was sexually assaulted by multiple members of the Chi Phi fraternity at a fraternity-house party in October 2024, followed by university disciplinary proceedings, civil litigation, and renewed criminal scrutiny. The allegations remain allegations; as of November 7, 2026, New York’s Office of the Attorney General had been appointed special prosecutor and had retained outside counsel to lead its criminal investigation.

facts.label: Alleged incident
facts.value: The alleged assault was reported as occurring at Cornell’s Chi Phi fraternity house between October 19 and October 20, 2024, in Ithaca, New York.

facts.label: University process
facts.value: Cornell issued a formal Title IX complaint against seven fraternity members on November 22, 2024; the university says its investigation and hearings resulted in expulsions and suspensions, though it does not publicly identify individual outcomes.

facts.label: Fraternity status
facts.value: Cornell says the Chi Phi Xi chapter was closed in 2024 and remains barred from campus.

facts.label: Criminal-investigation authority
facts.value: On October 1, 2026, Governor Kathy Hochul appointed the New York Attorney General’s Office as special prosecutor to investigate the allegations and, if warranted, present evidence to a grand jury and prosecute offenses arising from them.

facts.label: Independent institutional review
facts.value: Cornell’s Board of Trustees retained Sally Yates and King & Spalding to independently review the university’s prevention and response practices, including its handling of the 2024 Chi Phi allegations, against Title IX, Clery Act, Campus SaVE Act, state-law, and best-practice standards.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the late-September to mid-October 2026 reopening, institutional-response, lawsuit, and campus-governance developments; it does not constitute a complete evidentiary record or resolve the civil claims, university findings, or criminal investigation.

related_stories.title: Jay Rockefeller, Former Governor and Senator, Passes Away at 89
related_stories.summary: Jay Rockefeller, the last member of his family's political dynasty, has died at the age of 89. He served as the governor of West Virginia and was a longtime U.S. senator, known for his advocacy on healthcare, education, and working families' needs. Rockefeller was born into a prominent family and forged a significant political career.

related_stories.title: Momentum Builds for Coalition Talks in Israel as Eisenkot Gains Support
related_stories.summary: Following inconclusive elections, opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot is gaining momentum in his efforts to form a government in Israel. He has received significant backing, including from Arab parties, as President Isaac Herzog prepares to announce who will be tasked with forming the new government. Eisenkot aims to replace long-serving Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

related_stories.title: ANC Faces Significant Decline in South African Local Elections
related_stories.summary: The African National Congress (ANC) is projected to receive less than a third of the vote in South Africa's local elections, marking a significant decline from previous years. With over 80% of ballots counted, the ANC is on track for its worst-ever election performance, estimated at around 32%. This decline is attributed to widespread voter dissatisfaction over issues such as water outages and power cuts, leading to potential coalition challenges in major cities like Johannesburg and Tshwane.

related_stories.title: New Zealand General Election Results Leave Parliament Divided
related_stories.summary: The New Zealand general election has concluded without a clear winner, resulting in a highly divided parliament. Preliminary results show the two main parties nearly deadlocked in the popular vote, leading to expectations of extended coalition negotiations. Minor parties, including the Opportunity Party, may play a crucial role in forming a government.
